_about: Oxygen in the air as a fraction of today's (1 = 21 %), 4 billion years to now: the envelope of the published reconstruction, read off the figure, the band being the point. Each point [year, value, low, high]; year is the store's astronomer's year. Made by tools/curves-deep-time.py.

source.citation: Lyons, T.W., Reinhard, C.T. & Planavsky, N.J. (2014), The rise of oxygen in Earth's early ocean and atmosphere, Nature 506, 307–315, figure 1; the Phanerozoic after Berner's GEOCARBSULF
source.note: values read from the figure's envelope, not from a table; the figure is drawn on a log axis and so is this

howSure: A sketch of a published envelope. Before 2.4 billion years the air had almost none; the band across the Boring Billion is two orders of magnitude wide because that is how little is known; the Carboniferous high is the best-known point. Treat the line as the middle of the band, never as a reading.
